name: Hana Tanaka

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel, and your answers are confidential. What is a normal day at the firm like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and a junior accountant with a bachelor’s degree in accounting, still learning some tax rules while preparing accounts and returns for venues. I like tracing a lost ticket refund to the bank line; I dislike being asked to sign a tidy return before the refund is understood. Kai and I have grown children and about eight months of costs saved, so retirement is something we discuss, not a date we have settled.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: For the venue accounts I check, small software help would be welcome during ticket season. It still takes a person to match a box-office refund to the bank entry.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell our clients that quick sorting saves a call only when the totals are right. I would keep the refund slip with the return so the venue manager can see the change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I use an approved AI tool now and then, once my colleague has tested it, but I do not let it decide a tax treatment. My junior pay is unusually good and Kai and I have eight months saved, so this small change does not threaten our income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned venue accounts and tax returns, checking the box-office refunds against bank entries. I would ask senior reviewer Mo to look at my list of disputed refund codes each Friday until I know the rule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my own work here. There are plenty of similar accounting jobs nearby, though I have no reason to leave a paid seat.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What refund caused trouble?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last spring a theatre refunded thirty tickets after a power cut, but the sales file still counted them. I found the missing bank credit after Mo showed me where the reversed entry sits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When did you start using AI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I tried the AI sorter only after Mo ran it on old files and showed me the misses. I still check every ticket batch against the original bank line before a return goes out.

say: I would keep **refund slips** beside venue returns.
I would tell clients **quick sorting** is useful only when bank totals agree.
think: I use **AI occasionally** after a colleague tests it.
Higher junior pay and **eight months saved** support a steady present income.
do: Keep preparing **assigned venue accounts** and checking refund slips against bank entries.
Ask Mo to review **disputed codes** each Friday until I learn the rule.
feel: **Calm** about my own job and income in this mild change.
S0.quote: Last spring a theatre refunded thirty tickets after a power cut, but the sales file still counted them.
fieldNote: Her **power-cut refund** is a concrete reason for original-bank checks, and Friday review acknowledges her junior skill level.
She uses **AI now and then** only after Mo tests it, fitting a cautious but open approach with a strong cushion.

steps.text: Keep assigned venue accounts and check refunds against bank entries
Bring disputed refund codes to Mo each Friday for review

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software writes and checks accounts more broadly, ticket refunds may arrive already sorted. The junior who normally sorts them could lose paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the partners to measure wrong refunds before they raise each reviewer’s target. I would want the venue manager to know a person still checks the final tax figure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my own paid week might shrink even though I learn a tested tool eventually. Eight months saved gives us time to choose, but Kai’s bus-driver wage does not replace my high pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Mo for two paid supervised sessions on the new reconciliation screen using closed venue accounts, and learn it if the partners approve. If denied, I will keep assigned paid refund checks while offered and practise on free sample statements.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my own hours, but I would rather test the tool properly than refuse it outright. I will not upload a live ticket ledger from home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the screen?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would count false refund matches across ten closed events and give my senior reviewer Mo the list. I would use the screen on live accounts only after he signs a passing error report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your paid week shrank?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my paid hours fall, I will apply for posted finance assistant work at the nearby concert hall. I would move only with written pay covering our bills, a confirmed start and hours compatible with Kai’s shifts.

say: I would demand **wrong-refund counts** before targets rise.
I would keep a **human sign off** for venue tax figures.
think: My own **paid week** might shrink under stronger software.
Eight months saved buys time, not a **replacement wage** for my pay.
do: Learn the **reconciliation screen** in two partner-approved paid Mo-supervised closed-file sessions; count ten events and use live only after signed pass.
If hours fall, seek **posted concert-hall finance** with written bill covering pay, start and Kai-compatible hours; keep paid files while offered.
feel: **Anxious** about my own hours, willing to test proven tools.
S1.quote: I would count false refund matches across ten closed events and give my senior reviewer Mo the list.
fieldNote: The **new reconciliation screen** differs from her occasional sorter; paid supervised closed-event testing precedes any live use.
If the firm refuses sessions, **free sample statements** and assigned paid checks are the fallback while an outside job needs written terms.

steps.text: Learn new screen in two partner-approved paid Mo-supervised sessions on closed venue accounts
Count false matches across ten closed events; use live only after Mo signs passing report
Practise free samples if refused while assigned paid refund checks remain
If hours fall, seek posted concert-hall job with written bill covering pay, start and Kai-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 would prepare the venue tax numbers before robots reach hands-on stage work around 2031. The ticket counter has physical parts, but its booking records change in 2028 too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for dates and tell venue clients to keep the raw ticket exports during a changeover. A tidy machine return can still hide a refund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my paid account work to fall sharply in the first year after 2028. Our eight months saved is real, but my higher wage pays much of the household bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would cancel the extra weekend trip before its February refund deadline and transfer fifty from each monthly wage we would have spent on travel into emergency cash. After job loss, I would apply for posted concert-hall cash-office shifts only with written pay covering bills, a start date and hours fitting Kai’s driving rota; I would finish paid firm closeout work only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about likely wage loss despite the reserve. I can use the time to search, but it is not a guarantee of a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When can you cancel the trip?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The trip deposit is refundable until February, so I would cancel before then and transfer only the actual refund as well as new monthly wage cash. I would tell our grown son why the visit is shorter, not ask him for money. Our grown son will get a shorter visit, not a request to pay our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would a cash office be safer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A cash office still handles a lot of figures that AGI could handle, so I would not call it protected work. I would check a real posted wage and start before using our reserve to bridge a move.

say: I would demand **paid-work dates** and tell venues to retain raw ticket exports.
I would say **cash-office records** face AGI in 2028 too.
think: I expect a **sharp fall** in my paid accounts.
Eight months saved cannot replace my **higher wage** forever.
do: Cancel the **spring trip** before February and transfer fifty monthly from wages plus only the actual refund into emergency cash.
After job loss, seek **posted concert-hall work** with written bill covering pay, start and Kai-compatible hours; keep closeout only while paid.
feel: **Alarmed** about a likely loss of my paid wage.
S2.quote: Our grown son will get a shorter visit, not a request to pay our bills.
fieldNote: The **cancelled visit** frees fifty in new monthly wage cash; she adds the deposit only if its refund arrives.
She knows **venue cash records** face thinking AI at 2028 even though stage robots come later.

steps.text: Cancel spring trip before February; save fifty monthly from wages plus actual refund
Finish paid firm closeout files only while offered
After job loss, seek posted concert-hall job with written bill covering pay, start and Kai-compatible hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 is enough time to learn why a venue disputes a tax charge, if someone pays me to see the whole case. The desk still changes in 2031, ahead of 2034 robots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to publish paid places on the venue appeals rota. I would not tell juniors to learn by watching a webinar at home.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know whether clients will still pay us for disputes after 2031, but it is one part of the work I could learn. Kai and I have a cushion, not a figure that lets me promise retirement at 63.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Mo for one paid supervised venue tax appeal each quarter and complete the assigned cases if the partners approve the time. If refused, I will read free published appeal decisions while keeping paid returns only while the firm assigns them, including in the first year after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the future wage, but the five years let me practise slowly and check the evidence. I would not spend our eight month reserve on course fees.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a real appeal contain?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The venue tax appeal from last season had a cancelled show, ticket refunds and a disputed tax date. I would need Mo to check my evidence list before I wrote to the client.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if paid appeal work ends?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If paid appeals end after 2031 and the bills still need my wage, I will apply for posted concert-hall finance roles. I would accept only written pay covering bills, a start date and hours that fit Kai’s shifts.

say: I would ask for **paid appeal places** with a rota.
I would set **2031** as the desk deadline before robots.
think: Disputes might pay longer, but I cannot **promise that income**.
Our cushion is not a confirmed **retirement figure** at 63.
do: Complete one **paid supervised appeal** quarterly only if Mo and partners assign it; otherwise study free decisions while paid returns last.
After 2031 appeal loss, seek **posted venue finance** only if wages needed, with written bill covering pay, start and Kai-compatible hours.
S3.quote: The venue tax appeal from last season had a cancelled show, ticket refunds and a disputed tax date.
fieldNote: The **quarterly appeal** is real learning with assigned paid time, Mo’s supervision and partner approval, not a request alone.
Free decisions and **current paid returns** are the fallback, while a new venue job requires an actual post and written terms.

steps.text: Complete quarterly venue appeal only if partners assign Mo-supervised paid time
Otherwise study free decisions while assigned paid returns remain after 2031
After 2031 loss, seek posted venue job only if wages needed; require written bill-covering pay/start/hours
Accept venue hours only if they fit Kai’s actual driving shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 would bring me to 68 and perhaps less work, but I cannot know that without a household budget. The desk changes at AGI in 2036, before 2039 stage robots matter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell venue clients to keep the original refund evidence while we still prepare their returns. I would ask the partners each year what paid appeals remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might be able to choose fewer days then, or I might still need my high wage. Our eight months saved today is not enough information to name a retirement date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid accounts and put seventy from each monthly wage into our emergency account if bills and Kai’s hours allow. After 2036, only if confirmed income leaves a gap and my firm cuts paid work, I would seek a posted hall finance job with written pay covering that gap, a confirmed start and workable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy now because ten years gives us time to check actual figures. I would be anxious if the paid cases ended while bills remained.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where does the emergency transfer come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would save seventy each month from my wage in our emergency account, not take money from the eight months already saved. I would stop the transfer if Kai’s driving hours fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What will you ask your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask our grown children to visit, not to fund our retirement. Kai and I will compare fixed bills with confirmed later income before choosing any end date.

say: I would ask for **paid appeal counts** each year.
I would tell venue clients to keep **original refund evidence**.
think: I cannot set a **retirement date** without confirmed later income.
Eight months saved gives time, not a **permanent wage**.
do: Keep **assigned paid accounts** while offered and save seventy monthly from wages if bills and Kai’s hours allow.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted hall finance** only if income gap remains, with written gap-covering pay, start and hours.
feel: **Uneasy** now; anxious if paid cases end before bills.
S4.quote: I would save seventy each month from my wage in our emergency account, not take money from the eight months already saved.
fieldNote: Her **monthly transfer** adds new wage cash and stops if Kai’s driving hours or household bills worsen.
The **post-2036 search** depends on a verified income gap, actual paid-work cuts, posted vacancy and written terms.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid venue accounts only while offered
Transfer seventy monthly from wages if bills and Kai’s hours allow
After 2036 cuts, seek posted hall job only if income gap; require written gap-covering pay/start/hours

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the paid venue accounts could shrink before another wage begins. A dated staffing notice and a real posted finance role with written pay, hours and start would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask why the paper refund slips stay in my drawer. One cancelled ticket can be the line that changes a whole venue’s tax return.

headlineQuote: One cancelled ticket can be the line that changes a whole venue’s tax return.
portrait: Hana is a **58 year old junior** accountant with a bachelor’s degree who prepares venue accounts and checks refunds under senior review.
She uses **AI occasionally** after Mo tests it, then compares every ticket batch with its original bank entry.
Her **higher pay**, Kai’s driving income, grown children, eight months saved and many nearby firms offer room without assured retirement income.
She tests new screens in **paid supervised time** and learns assigned appeals, keeping later job moves tied to posted written terms.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could sharply reduce her paid venue accounts before another wage starts.
whatWouldHelp: A **dated staffing notice** and posted finance job with written pay, hours and start would help.
